items.d: to feel happy about something that will happen
items.ex: I'm looking forward to meeting you next week.

items.d: to discover information
items.ex: I called the station to find out when the last train leaves.

items.d: to stop doing or trying something
items.ex: She gave up smoking ten years ago.

items.d: to continue
items.ex: Carry on with your work while I make a phone call.

items.d: to start a business or organisation; to prepare equipment
items.ex: They set up a small bakery in their village.

items.d: to refuse an offer; to make quieter
items.ex: He turned down the job because the salary was too low.

items.d: to think of an idea or plan
items.ex: We need to come up with a better solution.

items.d: to delay doing something
items.ex: Don't put off your homework until Sunday night.

items.d: to have a good relationship with someone; to continue doing something
items.ex: I get on well with my colleagues.

items.d: to take care of
items.ex: My mother looks after my children when I'm at work.

items.d: to search for information in a dictionary or online
items.ex: If you don't know a word, look it up.

items.d: to have no more of something
items.ex: We've run out of milk, so I'll buy some.

items.d: to raise a child; to mention a subject
items.ex: She was brought up by her grandparents.

items.d: to start a new hobby or activity
items.ex: I took up yoga last year to reduce stress.

items.d: to do or use less of something
items.ex: I'm trying to cut down on sugar.

items.d: to take action to solve a problem
items.ex: The council must deal with the traffic problem.

items.d: to understand or solve something after thinking
items.ex: I can't figure out how this machine works.

items.d: to tell someone about a fact or problem
items.ex: My teacher pointed out a mistake in my essay.

items.d: to happen in a particular way; to be discovered to be
items.ex: The weather turned out better than we expected.

items.d: to finally be in a place or situation, often without planning
items.ex: We got lost and ended up in a small village.

items.d: to calculate or solve; to exercise
items.ex: Can you work out how much we owe?

items.d: to continue; to happen
items.ex: What's going on outside?

items.d: to collect someone or something; to learn something informally
items.ex: I picked up some Spanish while I was living in Madrid.

items.d: to invent a story or excuse; to form a whole
items.ex: Women make up 60% of the staff.

items.d: to do something good to correct a bad situation
items.ex: He bought her flowers to make up for being late.

items.d: to move or learn at the same speed as someone or something
items.ex: It's hard to keep up with changes in technology.

items.d: to reach the same level as others
items.ex: I missed a week of classes, so I need to catch up.

items.d: to fail to keep up with work or others
items.ex: Students who miss classes often fall behind.

items.d: to arrive, often unexpectedly or late
items.ex: Only half of the guests showed up.

items.d: to recover from an illness or a bad experience
items.ex: It took her months to get over the flu.

items.d: to stop working (machines); to lose control of emotions
items.ex: Our car broke down on the motorway.

items.d: to cancel an event
items.ex: The match was called off because of the rain.

items.d: to complete a form with information
items.ex: Please fill in this application form.

items.d: to give work to a teacher or person in authority
items.ex: You must hand in your essay by Friday.

items.d: to register for a course or activity
items.ex: I signed up for an evening English course.

items.d: to register at a hotel or airport
items.ex: We checked in two hours before the flight.

items.d: to start a journey
items.ex: We set off early to avoid the traffic.

items.d: to manage with difficulty, especially with money or language
items.ex: I know enough French to get by on holiday.

items.d: to depend on someone or something
items.ex: Many people rely on public transport to get to work.

items.d: to form a part of a total; to explain
items.ex: Tourism accounts for 15% of the country's income.

items.d: to cause a particular situation
items.ex: Heavy rain resulted in serious flooding.

items.d: to be caused by
items.ex: Many health problems stem from poor diet.

items.d: to stop using something gradually
items.ex: The government plans to phase out petrol cars.

items.d: to take control of something
items.ex: A large company took over the local factory.

items.d: to investigate
items.ex: The police are looking into the accident.

items.d: to experience something difficult; to examine carefully
items.ex: The country went through a difficult period.

items.d: to find or meet by chance
items.ex: I came across an old photo of my grandparents.

items.d: to accept something unpleasant without complaining
items.ex: I can't put up with this noise any longer.

items.d: to manage without something
items.ex: Most people can't do without their phones.

items.d: to solve a problem or organise something
items.ex: I need to sort out my visa before I travel.

items.d: to support; to make a copy of computer data
items.ex: Always back up your files.

items.d: to stop a supply; to isolate
items.ex: The village was cut off by snow for three days.

items.d: to become slower
items.ex: Economic growth slowed down last year.

items.d: to increase
items.ex: House prices have gone up a lot.

items.d: to decrease
items.ex: The number of visitors went down in winter.

items.d: to stop rising or falling and stay the same
items.ex: Sales rose quickly and then levelled off.

items.d: to consider carefully before deciding
items.ex: Think it over and give me your answer tomorrow.

items.d: to persuade someone to do something
items.ex: My friend talked me into joining the gym.

items.d: to be easy to notice; to be better than others
items.ex: Her application stood out from the rest.

items.d: to make an idea understood
items.ex: He used pictures to get his message across.

items.d: to start living a calm life in one place
items.ex: After years of travelling, they settled down in a small town.

items.d: to change from a child to an adult
items.ex: I grew up in a small village near the sea.

items.d: to start living in a new home
items.ex: We moved in last month and we're still unpacking.

items.d: to throw away or remove something unwanted
items.ex: I got rid of all my old clothes.

items.d: to put something in the rubbish
items.ex: Don't throw away plastic bottles; recycle them.

items.d: to participate
items.ex: Over 500 runners took part in the race.

items.d: to wait for a short time
items.ex: Hold on, I'll check my diary.

items.d: to start to have an illness
items.ex: I think I'm coming down with a cold.

items.d: to think you are better than someone
items.ex: He looks down on people without a degree.

items.d: to be as good as expected
items.ex: The hotel didn't live up to our expectations.
